Case Study: Table Data Version Identification

Using the GTSKB knowledge base and machine learning to automatically identify geologic time scale versions in legacy tabular data

Background

Geological literature often contains tables of fossil or lithology observations with stratigraphic period/stage names but rarely specifies which time scale version was used. The GTSKB knowledge base encodes boundary ages for over 100 versions (1879–2024), which can be used as a lookup oracle to match period/stage names to version-specific numeric ages. Combined with spatial (lat/lon) and lithological features, a machine learning model can be trained to automatically classify legacy records into the correct time scale version.

Methodology

1
Raw Data Parsing
Parse Excel records with Period, Stage, LMU, Lithology, Lat/Lon, Country, Continent, and Publication Year
2
KG Boundary Lookup
Query GTSKB TTL files by version + period/stage name to retrieve numeric age boundaries and uncertainties
3
Feature Encoding
Label-encode categorical features (Country, Continent, LMU, Period, Stage, Lithology); KNN-impute missing values
4
ML Classification
Train K-Nearest Neighbors (k=1) on encoded features; predict the time scale version for test records

Key Code

# Query KG for boundary ages of a period/stage in a specific version
def get_boundary_value(version_value, label):
    graph = Graph()
    graph.parse(f'{version_value}.ttl', format='ttl')
    start = graph.value(subject=URIRef(f'utf#{label}'), predicate=URIRef('utf#start'))
    end   = graph.value(subject=URIRef(f'utf#{label}'), predicate=URIRef('utf#end'))
    return start, end

# Encode categoricals + train KNN classifier
code, feat, test_feat = convert_to_category(training_data, test_data)
imp  = KNNImputer(n_neighbors=3).fit_transform(feat)
clf  = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=1).fit(imp, version_labels)
pred = clf.predict(test_feat)   # → version assignments for 2,479 test records
